anchors.paper_title: Estimating endogenous changes in task performance from EEG
anchors.reason: Touryan et al. 2014 (same BCIT authors) estimates EEG-based performance in simulated driving; it is topically close but not clearly the Traffic Complexity dataset's data paper.

anchors.paper_title: Event-related alpha perturbations related to the scaling of steering wheel corrections
anchors.reason: Brooks & Kerick 2015 studies alpha ERSP and steering corrections in driving from same lab/authors, but it's a separate research study, not a description of the BCIT Traffic Complexity dataset.

anchors.paper_title: Estimating direction in brain-behavior interactions: Proactive and reactive brain states in driving
anchors.reason: Garcia et al. 2017 is an analysis study of brain-behavior direction in driving EEG from the same lab (Brooks, Kerick, Johnson); it is not a data descriptor for the Traffic Complexity dataset.

anchors.paper_title: Automated EEG mega-analysis I: Spectral and amplitude characteristics across studies
anchors.reason: Mega-analysis paper presenting an automated EEG processing pipeline applied across 18 studies; an analysis-method paper, not a description of the Traffic Complexity dataset.

anchors.paper_title: Automated EEG mega-analysis II: Cognitive aspects of event related features
anchors.reason: Multi-study EEG mega-analysis (17 studies, HED tags) that likely includes BCIT data, but it is not this Traffic Complexity dataset's data paper; it is an analysis paper, so ambiguous evidence favors related_work.

anchors.paper_title: Novel Measure of Driver and Vehicle Interaction Demonstrates Transient Changes Related to Alerting
anchors.reason: Brooks et al. 2014 introduces a driving steering measure (RSWC) from a driving study with verbal queries; it does not describe the Traffic Complexity dataset itself, so it is only topically related.

metadata.methods_description: Participants drove in a simulator (steering wheel and pedals) on a long straight road and corrected lateral perturbations to stay in the right-most lane. Recordings included 64-channel BioSemi EEG (plus 4 eye and 2 mastoid channels, 2048 Hz), SMI REDEYE250 eye tracking, and vehicle logs at 100 Hz. Task order versus Baseline Driving was counter-balanced. Fatigue and sleepiness questionnaires (TIFS, KSS, VAS-F) were collected.
